# FamilyFooter

The foot of a family's site: the `FamilyBar`'s links, in the same order, in a quiet row that wraps, with the site being shown marked the same way, and the site's own extras (`children`) after them. The family's links are a labelled `<nav>` of plain links, whole in the server HTML.

```tsx
import { FamilyFooter } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/family-bar/family-footer";
```

## Example

```tsx
<FamilyFooter links={sites} current="docs">
  <Link href="/privacy" tone="secondary">Privacy</Link>
  <Link href="/terms" tone="secondary">Terms</Link>
</FamilyFooter>
```

## Use instead when

- Use `FamilyBar` instead for the strip above the site's header, and `Navbar` for a site's own pages.

## Props

Type: `FamilyFooterProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The site's own extras, after the family's links: its Privacy and Terms links, a line about who makes it. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, grid placement (`mt-auto`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `current` | `string` |  | The `id` of the site being shown, marked as in the `FamilyBar`: `aria-current="true"`, heavier text and a bar under it. |
| `label` | `string` | `"All sites"` | Names the footer's navigation for screen readers, apart from the bar's. It is not shown. |
| `links` (required) | `readonly FamilyLink[]` |  | The family's sites, in order: the list the site's `FamilyBar` takes. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `currentPath`: Not a prop. FamilyFooter marks a site by its id, not by a path: `<FamilyFooter current="docs">`.
- `items`: Not a prop. FamilyFooter takes `links`: `<FamilyFooter links={[{ id: "docs", label: "Docs", href: "/" }]} />`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `FamilyLink`

One site of a family, in a FamilyBar and a FamilyFooter.

```ts
interface FamilyLink {
  /** Names the site for `current`: "docs". It is not shown. */
  id: string;
  /** The site's name, the link's text: "Docs". */
  label: string;
  /** Where the link goes: the site's home page, "https://docs.example.com/". */
  href: string;
}
```
